hero.lead: HALALNiaga is a digital halal ecosystem for small food vendors — connecting nearby verified suppliers of fresh wet ingredients, practical training and a traceable record customers can scan at the stall.
hero.disclaimer: Programme recognition only. HALALNiaga does not issue halal certification — that remains with JAKIM and the state Islamic authorities.

problems.title: Suppliers are hard to verify
problems.body: Certificates sit in drawers or inboxes, rarely at the 6am wet-market decision about which chicken, fish or vegetable crate to buy.

problems.title: Halal knowledge is uneven
problems.body: Many vendors still reduce halal to “no pork, no alcohol”, missing slaughter, storage and separation.

problems.title: Certification feels out of reach
problems.body: A small stall assumes the official process is too complex or expensive to even explore.

problems.title: Purchase records do not exist
problems.body: Without receipts or supplier references, nobody can prove where the chicken, fish or produce came from.

problems.title: Cross-contamination is invisible
problems.body: Shared boards, knives and oil are common — and almost never documented or corrected.

problems.title: Wet ingredients move faster than paperwork
problems.body: Chicken, fish, vegetables, eggs and milk are bought several times a week, often from different stalls. A record built for monthly invoices cannot keep up with a wet market.

modules.title: Halal supplier finder
modules.description: Search certified and verified suppliers of fresh poultry, meat, seafood, produce, dairy and eggs by area — with a nearest-first list and a wet-ingredients filter.

modules.title: Halal education & training
modules.description: Six short modules written for busy stalls — foundations, slaughter, ingredients, separation, storage and records.

modules.title: Purchase tracking
modules.description: Every receipt becomes evidence: supplier, product, quantity, date and source reference in one traceable log.

modules.title: Self-assessment
modules.description: A recurring eight-point check that surfaces the weakest control and tells the vendor what to fix next.

modules.title: QR verification
modules.description: A stall-side QR opens the vendor’s programme record — training, sourcing, assessment and last inspection.

modules.title: Monitoring & recognition
modules.description: Inspections and re-assessment move vendors through three recognition tiers, with validity periods that expire.

steps.title: Register the stall
steps.body: Owner, location, menu and the ingredients that matter most.

steps.title: Complete halal training
steps.body: Six practical modules, then a scored quiz for each one.

steps.title: Source with evidence
steps.body: Find verified suppliers and attach every purchase to a source.

steps.title: Assess and correct
steps.body: Run the self-assessment, see the weakest control, close the gap.

steps.title: Earn recognition
steps.body: Publish a QR record, then maintain it through inspections.

tiers.title: Learner
criteria: Training record signed by the programme

tiers.title: Verified participant
criteria: At least 80% of recent purchases from verified suppliers

tiers.title: Monitored participant
criteria: Programme inspection passed within six months

beneficiaries.benefit: A practical route to maintain halal practice, with the evidence built into daily work.
Clear guidance and a fair, compliance-based route to serve Muslim customers.
A QR check at the stall instead of relying on a logo or a rumour.
A new, reachable market of small vendors looking for trustworthy sources.
Better records, targeted education and a visible correction trail.
